a

The solar constant is the intensity of solar radiation received per unit area at the top of the Earth's atmosphere, measured on a surface perpendicular to the Sun's rays. However, the Earth is a sphere, so the solar radiation is spread over the entire surface area of the Earth, which is four times the cross-sectional area (the area of the Earth's shadow). Therefore, to get the average incoming intensity over the whole Earth, the solar constant must be divided by 4.
